2027-06-05.title: The Immaculate Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary · St Boniface
readings: I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my whole being shall exult in my God
My heart exults in the Lord
His mother treasured all these things in her heart
2027-06-05.alt: Saturday of the Ninth Week in Ordinary Time (Year I). The Immaculate Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary (Saturday after the Sacred Heart) and St Boniface, bishop and martyr, are both obligatory memorials; because they fall on the same day in 2027, by the rule for coinciding memorials both become optional this year (follow your diocesan Ordo). This page gives the readings of the Immaculate Heart. The weekday readings are Tobit 12:1, 5–15, 20 (Raphael reveals himself); the canticle Tobit 13:2, 6, 7, 8 (“Blessed be God, who lives forever”); and Mark 12:38–44 (the widow's two small coins). Also World Environment Day. Liturgical colour: white (red for St Boniface; green for the weekday).
2027-06-05.verse: Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart.
theo: Yesterday the Church contemplated the pierced Heart of the Son; today she turns to the Heart of his Mother, which was pierced too, as Simeon foretold: “a sword will pierce your own soul too” (Luke 2:35). The two feasts stand side by side because the two hearts were never apart. The first reading is a song of the restored Zion, the city God has rescued and adorned: “I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my whole being shall exult in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.” The Church has always heard Mary's voice in these words. She is the first of the redeemed, clothed in salvation from the first moment of her existence: that is what Immaculate means. Her heart was never stained by sin, not because she did not need a Saviour, but because the Saviour reached her first, in view of the merits of her Son. And Isaiah ends with an image of growth: “For as the earth brings forth its shoots, and as a garden causes what is sown in it to spring up, so the Lord God will cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations.” Mary's heart is that garden: the Word was sown in it, and it brought forth the Saviour. The responsorial psalm is the song of Hannah, the mother of Samuel: “My heart exults in the Lord; my strength is exalted in my God.” Hannah's song is the elder sister of Mary's Magnificat: “The barren has borne seven … He raises up the poor from the dust; he lifts the needy from the ash heap.” God lifts up the lowly, and Mary is the lowly one he lifted highest.

The Gospel is the only story of Jesus' boyhood in the Gospels. Every year Joseph and Mary go up to Jerusalem for the Passover. When Jesus is twelve, he stays behind in the city without telling them. They travel a day's journey, assuming he is with relatives, and then begin the long search. “After three days they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.” Mary speaks for both parents: “Child, why have you treated us like this? Look, your father and I have been searching for you in great anxiety.” Here we see the heart of Mary, not calm and untroubled, but anxious, searching, loving. The Immaculate Heart is not a heart that feels nothing; it is a heart that feels everything without sin. Jesus answers with his first recorded words: “Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?” And Luke adds honestly: “they did not understand what he said to them.” Mary does not understand, yet she does not stop believing. “Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart.” The Greek word means to keep carefully, to hold together, to ponder over time. Mary's heart is the place where the mysteries of Christ are kept and slowly understood. Before she conceived Christ in her womb, says St Augustine (in substance), she conceived him in her heart by faith. Devotion to her Immaculate Heart grew through St John Eudes in the seventeenth century and was given new urgency at Fatima in 1917; Pius XII consecrated the world to her Immaculate Heart in 1942 and in 1944 extended this feast to the whole Church. To honour her Heart is to learn from her how to keep the Word, how to search for Jesus when we have lost him, and how to stay faithful when we do not understand.

Today the Church could also keep the memorial of St Boniface, the apostle of Germany. Wynfrith, an English Benedictine monk, was sent by Pope Gregory II in 719 and given the name Boniface. He preached in Hesse and Thuringia, felled the sacred oak of Thor at Geismar to show that the old gods had no power, founded monasteries such as Fulda, and became archbishop of Mainz. In old age he went back to the Frisians, and on 5 June 754, near Dokkum, he and his companions were killed by a band of raiders; tradition says he raised a book of the Gospels over his head. The weekday readings, if they are used, end the story of Tobit: Raphael reveals himself, “I am Raphael, one of the seven angels who stand ready and enter before the glory of the Lord,” and teaches that “almsgiving saves from death and purges away every sin”; and in the Gospel Jesus praises the poor widow who gave “everything she had, all she had to live on.” Mary, the widow, and Boniface each gave God everything. And on this World Environment Day, Isaiah's garden reminds us that the earth that brings forth its shoots is God's gift, to be tended with care.
conn: “A sword will pierce your own soul too.”
Simeon's words to Mary (Luke 2:35) unite the two feasts of these days: the pierced Heart of the Son and the sorrowful Heart of the Mother.
“As a bride adorns herself with her jewels.”
Isaiah 61:10. The Church sees in the adorned bride both Zion and Mary, the first of the redeemed, clothed in salvation from her conception (Catechism 490–492).
“As a garden causes what is sown in it to spring up.”
Isaiah 61:11. The Fathers called Mary a garden enclosed (Song of Songs 4:12), in which the Word was sown and the Saviour sprang up.
Hannah's song.
1 Samuel 2:1–10 is the model of Mary's Magnificat (Luke 1:46–55): both praise the God who lifts the lowly and fills the hungry.
Twelve years old.
At about this age a Jewish boy began to take on the obligations of the Law. Jesus' first recorded words are about his Father: “I must be in my Father's house.”
“After three days.”
The three days of searching foreshadow the three days between the Cross and the Resurrection, when Mary would again lose and find her Son.
“They did not understand.”
Mary walked by faith, not by sight; she advanced in her “pilgrimage of faith” (Lumen Gentium 58), keeping what she did not yet understand.
“Treasured all these things in her heart.”
Luke says it twice (2:19 and 2:51). Mary is the first contemplative of the Gospel, the memory of the Church.
The widow's two coins.
The weekday Gospel (Mark 12:41–44): Jesus praises a poor widow who gave all she had. Mary too gave all, her Son, at the foot of the Cross.
The memorial.

St John Eudes promoted the liturgical honour of the Heart of Mary in the seventeenth century. Pius XII extended the feast to the whole Church in 1944; since 1969 it is kept on the Saturday after the Sacred Heart, and St John Paul II made it an obligatory memorial in 1996.
altar: Mary kept the words of Jesus in her heart; at Mass we receive the Word made flesh into our own hearts. She is the model of every good Communion: welcome him with faith, keep him with love, ponder him in silence.

In Eucharistic Prayer I the Church names first among the saints “the glorious ever-Virgin Mary, Mother of our God and Lord, Jesus Christ.” At every altar the Mother stands where she stood on Calvary, beside the sacrifice of her Son, and teaches us to offer ourselves with him.
outline: Ask: where do you keep the things that matter most to you? Mary kept them in her heart.
Point 1 · A heart clothed with salvation
Isaiah's bride and Hannah's song: Mary, the first of the redeemed, the lowly one lifted up.
Three days of anxiety: the Immaculate Heart feels everything, without sin.
Not understanding, she treasures and ponders.
Point 4 · A heart that gives everything
The widow's coins, Boniface's martyrdom, Mary's Son.
A mother in Nazareth at night, the lamp burning low, turning over in her heart the words of her twelve-year-old son.
“His mother treasured all these things in her heart.”
live: Make or renew an act of consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary today, alone or with your family.
Begin the five First Saturdays asked at Fatima: confession, Holy Communion, five decades of the Rosary and fifteen minutes meditating on its mysteries, in reparation to her Immaculate Heart.
Choose one sentence from today's Gospel and carry it in your heart all day, as Mary did.
On World Environment Day, do one practical thing for God's creation: plant a tree, refuse plastic, or save water as the monsoon begins.
fathers: Mary is more blessed in receiving the faith of Christ than in conceiving the flesh of Christ. Her motherhood would have profited her nothing had she not borne Christ in her heart more happily than in her flesh (On Holy Virginity 3).

Mary kept all the words in her heart, not only what she understood but also what she did not yet understand, comparing them with what she had read in the prophets, waiting for the time when they would be made clear (Homilies on the Gospels).
The Heart of Mary is wholly given to the Heart of Jesus; whoever honours her Heart honours the Heart of her Son, who lives and reigns in it.
magis: The finding of Jesus in the Temple: Mary and Joseph did not understand, but accepted in faith; and Mary kept all these things in her heart during the years Jesus remained hidden in the silence of an ordinary life.
Jesus learned to pray in his human heart from his mother, who kept all the great things the Almighty had done and treasured them in her heart.
Mary's prayer is revealed at the dawning of the fullness of time: her Fiat and her Magnificat.
The Mother's union with her Son: when he was found in the Temple his parents did not understand, and his mother kept all these things in her heart; she advanced in her pilgrimage of faith.
In the midst of the Second World War Pius XII consecrated the Church and the human race to the Immaculate Heart of Mary; in 1944 he extended this feast to the universal Church.
saints: Born Wynfrith in Wessex, England, he became a Benedictine monk. In 719 Pope Gregory II gave him the name Boniface and sent him to preach to the Germanic peoples. Ordained bishop in 722, he felled the sacred oak of Thor at Geismar, founded monasteries including Fulda (744), reformed the Frankish Church and became archbishop of Mainz. Returning in old age to Frisia, he was killed with his companions near Dokkum on 5 June 754. He is buried at Fulda and honoured as the Apostle of Germany.

6 Jun: Tenth Sunday in Ordinary Time. 9 Jun: St Ephrem, deacon and doctor. 11 Jun: St Barnabas, apostle. The weekday readings of the coming week begin the Second Letter to the Corinthians and the Sermon on the Mount.
2027-06-05.prayer: O God, who prepared a fit dwelling place for the Holy Spirit in the Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary, graciously grant that through her intercession we may be a worthy temple of your glory. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Immaculate Heart of Mary, you kept every word of your Son and treasured what you did not yet understand; teach us to search for Jesus when we have lost him, to keep his word, and to give him everything. Through the prayers of St Boniface, make us brave witnesses to the Gospel. Amen.

quick: Isaiah sings of Zion clothed in salvation like a bride, and Hannah of the God who lifts the lowly: the Church hears in both the voice of Mary.
Mary and Joseph search for the twelve-year-old Jesus for three days and find him in his Father's house; they do not understand, but his mother treasured all these things in her heart.
St Boniface, apostle of Germany, was martyred at Dokkum on 5 June 754; the weekday Gospel praises the widow who gave all she had.
2027-06-05.action: Renew your consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary today, and carry one word of the Gospel in your heart all day.
2027-06-05.question: When I do not understand what God is doing, do I keep and ponder, or do I complain and walk away?
catechism: The finding of Jesus in the Temple.
Jesus learns to pray from the heart of his mother.
Mary, full of grace, preserved from all stain of sin.
kidsaint: Boniface was a monk from England who went to Germany to tell people about Jesus. Many people there worshipped a huge old oak tree, thinking a god called Thor lived in it. Boniface took an axe and cut the tree down! Nothing bad happened to him, and the people saw that the true God is stronger. He used the wood to build a little chapel. When he was very old, he was killed by robbers while he was getting ready to confirm new Christians. Lesson: be brave to show people that Jesus is the true God.
2027-06-05.special: The Immaculate Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary and St Boniface, bishop and martyr: two obligatory memorials falling on the same day, so both optional in 2027 (follow the diocesan Ordo). World Environment Day.
term: The heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary, never touched by sin, because she was preserved from original sin from the first moment of her conception by the grace of God in view of the merits of Christ (Pius IX, Ineffabilis Deus, 1854). In devotion the “heart” means the whole inner person: her faith, love, sorrow and contemplation. To honour her Immaculate Heart is to honour her love for God and for us, and to learn from her how to keep the Word of God.

family.explain: When Jesus was twelve, he stayed in the Temple in Jerusalem, and Mary and Joseph searched for him for three days. When they found him, Jesus said that he had to be in his Father's house. Mary did not understand everything, but she kept it all in her heart and thought about it. Our Mother Mary's heart is full of love for Jesus and for us. She can help us when we feel lost.
family.intention: We pray for children who are lost or separated from their families, and for parents who are worried about their children.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing about Jesus we want to keep in our hearts this week, like Mary did?”

illus: A mother in Thiruvananthapuram kept a small notebook on her kitchen shelf. In it she wrote, over twenty years, things her children said about God: a question at bedtime, a prayer one of them made up, the day her son said he wanted to be a priest and the day he said he did not. When that son, grown up, was going through a dark time, she gave him the notebook. He read it in one night and came home the next Sunday. She said she had learned it from the Gospel: his mother treasured all these things in her heart. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Holy Mary, Mother of God, your Heart kept every word of your Son. Gather us around Jesus as you gathered the apostles, and teach us to keep his word. Amen.
share: He has clothed me with the garments of salvation (Isaiah 61:10). What does it mean for me that God has clothed me with salvation in Baptism?
Your father and I have been searching for you in great anxiety (Luke 2:48). When have I lost Jesus, and how did I find him again?
His mother treasured all these things in her heart (Luke 2:51). What word of God am I treasuring at this time of my life?
pm.resp: My heart exults in the Lord.
interc: For the Church, that like Mary she may keep the Word of God and ponder it in her heart.
For the world, consecrated to the Immaculate Heart of Mary, that peace may come where there is war.
For parents searching for children who have wandered away from God or from home.
For missionaries, through the prayers of St Boniface, that they may preach with courage.
For the care of creation on World Environment Day, that we may tend the earth as God's garden.
pm.close: Father, you gave Mary a heart that was wholly yours. Through her prayers, give us hearts that search for your Son, keep his word, and give him everything. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, yesterday we looked at the Heart of Jesus, pierced on the Cross. Today the Church invites us to look at the Heart of his Mother. These two feasts sit side by side because these two hearts were never separated. Simeon told Mary: a sword will pierce your own soul too (Luke 2:35). When the Son's Heart was pierced, the Mother's Heart was pierced with him.

Isaiah gives us a joyful picture: I will greatly rejoice in the Lord … for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation … as a bride adorns herself with her jewels (Isaiah 61:10). We hear Mary in these words. From the first moment of her life God clothed her with salvation and kept her heart pure from every sin. That is why we call her Heart Immaculate. And Hannah's song, which we prayed as the Psalm, is the mother of Mary's own Magnificat: my heart exults in the Lord.

But the Gospel shows us that an Immaculate Heart is not a heart without feelings. Mary loses her twelve-year-old son. For three days she searches, with Joseph, through the crowded city. When they find him, she says: Child, why have you treated us like this? Your father and I have been searching for you in great anxiety (Luke 2:48). Every mother who has waited at night for a child who did not come home knows that anxiety. Mary's Heart feels everything we feel, but without sin, without bitterness, without despair.

Then Jesus says something she does not understand: did you not know that I must be in my Father's house? And Luke says simply: his mother treasured all these things in her heart (Luke 2:51). She did not understand, but she did not throw the words away. She kept them, carried them, turned them over for years, until on Calvary and on Easter morning she understood. That is faith: keeping God's word even when we cannot see where it leads.

Today we could also remember St Boniface, who left England to bring the Gospel to Germany, cut down the oak that people worshipped, and was killed in his old age, raising the Gospel book over his head. And the weekday Gospel tells of a poor widow who gave everything she had. Mary, Boniface and the widow have one thing in common: they kept nothing back from God.

So let us consecrate ourselves today to the Immaculate Heart of Mary. When you lose Jesus, through sin or through busyness, search for him as she did, and you will find him in his Father's house, in the Church and in the Eucharist. When you do not understand what God is doing, keep his word in your heart as she did. And ask her to give you a heart like hers, wholly given to God. Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus was twelve years old, he got lost! Mary and Joseph searched for him for three whole days. Can you imagine how worried they were? At last they found him in the Temple, talking with the teachers about God.

Mary did not understand everything Jesus said, but she kept it all in her heart like a treasure. Our Mother Mary has a heart full of love. If you ever feel lost or sad, you can talk to her. She will always lead you back to Jesus.

intro: Theme: “His mother treasured all these things in her heart.”
The Immaculate Heart of Mary: clothed in salvation, searching in love, keeping the Word, and giving everything.

sub: Clothed with the garments of salvation.
q: My heart exults in the Lord; my strength is exalted in my God.
My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior,
points.apply: Begin each day this week by praying the Magnificat, slowly, and thank God for one way he has lifted you up.

q: I will rise now and go about the city, in the streets and in the squares; I will seek him whom my soul loves.
Child, why have you treated us like this? Look, your father and I have been searching for you in great anxiety.
points.apply: If you have drifted from Jesus, search for him this week where Mary found him: in his Father's house, at Mass and in confession.

q: I treasure your word in my heart, so that I may not sin against you.
Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart.
points.apply: Learn one verse of today's Gospel by heart and repeat it whenever you do not understand what God is doing.

q: It is better to give alms than to lay up gold.
For all of them have contributed out of their abundance; but she out of her poverty has put in everything she had, all she had to live on.
points.apply: Consecrate yourself and your family to the Immaculate Heart of Mary, and give one generous gift to someone in need.

concl: Mary's Heart is Immaculate not because it feels nothing, but because it feels everything with faith and love, without sin.
She teaches us to exult in God, to search for Jesus, to keep his word when we do not understand, and to give him everything.
2027-06-05.resolve: Make the five First Saturdays, beginning today if you can, and pray the Magnificat each morning this week.
